title: PowerShell Download Cradle Execution
description: Detects PowerShell processes using common download cradle patterns such as Invoke-Expression with web requests, DownloadString, or DownloadFile. These one-liners are the most frequent initial payload delivery mechanism observed in real-world intrusions.
kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("IEX", "Invoke-Expression", "Invoke-WebRequest", "Invoke-RestMethod", ".DownloadString", ".DownloadFile", "Start-BitsTransfer")
| where ProcessCommandLine !has "WindowsUpdate"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| sort by Timestamp desc
author: triathIC
tuning_notes: Exclude SCCM/Intune management scripts and known automation service accounts. Add org-specific update scripts to the !has filter.

title: PowerShell Encoded Command Execution Survey
description: Surveys all PowerShell executions using -EncodedCommand, -enc, or Base64-encoded inline scripts over the past 7 days. Useful for identifying obfuscated payloads that bypass simple string-matching detections.
kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("-enc", "-EncodedCommand", "-encodedcommand", "-ec ", "FromBase64String")
| summarize ExecutionCount = count(), Devices = dcount(DeviceName), Accounts = make_set(AccountName) by InitiatingProcessFileName, bin(Timestamp, 1d)
| sort by ExecutionCount desc
author: triathIC
tuning_notes: Environments with heavy PowerShell automation (DSC, SCCM) will generate high volume. Filter by InitiatingProcessFileName to isolate suspicious parent processes.

title: Cmd.exe Spawned by Suspicious Parent Process
description: Detects cmd.exe launched by processes commonly abused for initial execution such as mshta.exe, wscript.exe, cscript.exe, or rundll32.exe. This parent-child relationship is a strong indicator of script-based malware execution.
kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where FileName =~ "cmd.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("mshta.exe", "wscript.exe", "cscript.exe", "rundll32.exe", "regsvr32.exe", "wmiprvse.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| sort by Timestamp desc
author: triathIC

title: Cmd.exe with Obfuscated or Long Command Lines
description: Hunts for cmd.exe executions with unusually long command lines (>500 chars) or common obfuscation patterns (caret insertion, environment variable abuse). Long or obfuscated command lines are frequently used to evade static detection rules.
kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName =~ "cmd.exe"
| extend CmdLength = strlen(ProcessCommandLine)
| where CmdLength > 500 or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("^^^", "%comspec%", "cmd /V", "cmd /C set")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, CmdLength, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| sort by CmdLength desc
author: triathIC
tuning_notes: Adjust the CmdLength threshold based on your environment. Build automation and installer scripts can legitimately produce long command lines.

title: Successful Sign-in from Anonymizer or Tor Exit Node
description: Detects successful Azure AD sign-ins originating from known anonymizer networks or flagged as anonymous by Entra ID risk engine. Threat actors frequently use VPNs and Tor to access compromised accounts.
kql:
SigninLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ResultType == 0
| where RiskState == "atRisk" or NetworkLocationDetails has "anonymizer" or IPAddress has_any ("tor", "vpn")
| project TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, IPAddress, Location, AppDisplayName, RiskLevelDuringSignIn, ConditionalAccessStatus
| sort by TimeGenerated desc
author: triathIC
tuning_notes: Supplement with a custom watchlist of known Tor exit node IPs for more precise matching. The RiskState field depends on Entra ID P2 licensing.

title: Sign-ins from Multiple Countries Within Short Window
description: Hunts for user accounts that successfully authenticated from two or more distinct countries within a 4-hour window. This impossible-travel pattern indicates credential compromise or shared account abuse.
kql:
SigninLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ResultType == 0
| extend Country = tostring(LocationDetails.countryOrRegion)
| where isnotempty(Country)
| summarize Countries = dcount(Country), CountryList = make_set(Country), SignInCount = count() by UserPrincipalName, bin(TimeGenerated, 4h)
| where Countries >= 2
| sort by Countries desc
author: triathIC
tuning_notes: Exclude known traveling executives and VPN egress countries. Adjust the bin window (4h) based on organizational travel patterns.

title: Brute Force Against Single Account
description: Detects more than 10 failed sign-in attempts against a single user account within 15 minutes, followed by a successful sign-in. This pattern indicates a password spray or brute force that eventually succeeded.
kql:
let FailThreshold = 10;
let TimeWindow = 15m;
SigninLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| summarize FailCount = countif(ResultType != 0), SuccessCount = countif(ResultType == 0), IPAddresses = make_set(IPAddress) by UserPrincipalName, bin(TimeGenerated, TimeWindow)
| where FailCount >= FailThreshold and SuccessCount >= 1
| sort by FailCount desc
author: triathIC
tuning_notes: Adjust FailThreshold based on org size. Service accounts with misconfigured passwords may trigger false positives — consider excluding them by UPN pattern.

title: Distributed Password Spray Across Multiple Accounts
description: Hunts for a single IP address or small IP range attempting sign-ins against many distinct user accounts, indicating a distributed password spray. Attackers typically try one or two passwords against many accounts to stay below lockout thresholds.
kql:
SigninLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ResultType in ("50126", "50053", "50055")
| summarize TargetAccounts = dcount(UserPrincipalName), AccountList = make_set(UserPrincipalName, 20), AttemptCount = count() by IPAddress, bin(TimeGenerated, 1h)
| where TargetAccounts >= 10
| sort by TargetAccounts desc
author: triathIC
tuning_notes: ResultType 50126 = invalid password, 50053 = locked account, 50055 = expired password. Adjust TargetAccounts threshold based on org size.

title: Email with Suspicious Attachment File Type Delivered
description: Detects delivered emails containing attachment file types commonly used in spearphishing campaigns including macros, executables, ISO images, and shortcut files. These file types are the primary initial access vector for targeted attacks.
kql:
EmailEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
| join kind=inner EmailAttachmentInfo on NetworkMessageId
| where FileType in~ ("exe", "dll", "scr", "hta", "vbs", "js", "wsf", "iso", "img", "vhd", "lnk", "docm", "xlsm", "pptm")
| project Timestamp, SenderFromAddress, RecipientEmailAddress, Subject, FileName, FileType, SHA256, DeliveryAction
| sort by Timestamp desc
author: triathIC
tuning_notes: Expand or reduce the FileType list based on your org's email security policy. Consider excluding internal relay addresses from SenderFromAddress.

title: Attachment Delivered from First-Time External Sender
description: Identifies emails with attachments delivered from external senders who have never previously sent to the recipient. First-time senders with attachments are a common spearphishing vector worth reviewing in bulk.
kql:
let KnownSenders = EmailEvents
| where Timestamp between (ago(30d) .. ago(1d))
| where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
| distinct SenderFromAddress, RecipientEmailAddress;
EmailEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
| where SenderFromAddress !endswith "yourdomain.com"
| join kind=inner EmailAttachmentInfo on NetworkMessageId
| join kind=leftanti KnownSenders on SenderFromAddress, RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, SenderFromAddress, RecipientEmailAddress, Subject, FileName, FileType
| sort by Timestamp desc
author: triathIC
tuning_notes: Replace 'yourdomain.com' with your organization's actual email domain(s). The 30d lookback for KnownSenders can be adjusted based on data retention.

title: Scheduled Task Created via Schtasks.exe
description: Detects scheduled task creation using schtasks.exe with /create flag. Adversaries use scheduled tasks for persistence and privilege escalation by executing payloads at system startup or on a recurring schedule.
kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where FileName =~ "schtasks.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "/create"
| where ProcessCommandLine !has "Microsoft\\Windows"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| sort by Timestamp desc
author: triathIC
tuning_notes: The Microsoft\Windows exclusion filters standard OS tasks. Add exclusions for your patch management and endpoint management tooling (e.g., SCCM, Intune).

title: Scheduled Task Registration via Event Log
description: Hunts for scheduled task creation events (EventID 4698) in Windows Security logs over the past 7 days. Provides visibility into tasks created through any method including COM API, not just schtasks.exe.
kql:
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4698
| extend TaskName = tostring(EventData.TaskName), TaskContent = tostring(EventData.TaskContent)
| where TaskName !startswith "\\Microsoft\\Windows\\"
| summarize CreationCount = count() by TaskName, SubjectUserName, Computer, bin(TimeGenerated, 1d)
| sort by CreationCount desc
author: triathIC

title: RDP Connection to External IP Address
description: Detects outbound RDP connections (port 3389) to external (non-RFC1918) IP addresses. Legitimate RDP should be constrained to internal networks or managed gateways; external RDP indicates tunneling or unauthorized remote access.
kql:
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemotePort == 3389
| where ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| where not(ipv4_is_private(RemoteIP))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, InitiatingProcessFileName
| sort by Timestamp desc
author: triathIC

title: RDP Logon Sweep from Single Source
description: Identifies a single source account or IP performing RDP logons (Type 10) to multiple distinct machines within 7 days. This lateral movement pattern is common during post-compromise internal reconnaissance.
kql:
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4624
| where LogonType == 10
| summarize TargetMachines = dcount(Computer), MachineList = make_set(Computer, 25), LogonCount = count() by IpAddress, TargetUserName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1d)
| where TargetMachines >= 5
| sort by TargetMachines desc
author: triathIC
tuning_notes: IT admins and helpdesk accounts legitimately RDP to many machines. Exclude known admin accounts or raise TargetMachines threshold.

title: Mass File Encryption Detected — Ransomware Pattern
description: Detects rapid file rename operations appending known ransomware extensions or a single process renaming more than 50 files within 1 minute. This is a high-confidence indicator of active ransomware encryption and requires immediate response.
kql:
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where ActionType == "FileRenamed"
| where FileName endswith_any (".encrypted", ".locked", ".crypt", ".enc", ".ransom", ".zzz", ".locky", ".cerber", ".zepto", ".thor")
| summarize RenamedCount = count(), FilesSample = make_set(FileName, 10) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where RenamedCount >= 50
| sort by RenamedCount desc
author: triathIC
tuning_notes: Extend the endswith_any list with ransomware extensions relevant to current threat landscape. Legitimate encryption tools (7zip, BitLocker) should be excluded by InitiatingProcessFileName.

title: High Volume File Modifications by Single Process
description: Hunts for any single process modifying or creating an unusually high number of files across multiple directories within 30 days. Identifies both known ransomware patterns and novel encryption tools that do not use recognizable extensions.
kql:
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated", "FileModified", "FileRenamed")
| summarize FileCount = count(), UniqueDirectories = dcount(FolderPath), FileSample = make_set(FileName, 10) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1h)
| where FileCount >= 200 and UniqueDirectories >= 5
| sort by FileCount desc
author: triathIC

title: Registry Run Key Persistence Added
description: Detects new values written to common auto-start registry run keys. Adversaries add entries to these keys to maintain persistence across reboots.
kql:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where ActionType == "RegistryValueSet"
| where RegistryKey has_any ("\\CurrentVersion\\Run", "\\CurrentVersion\\RunOnce", "\\CurrentVersion\\RunOnceEx")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("msiexec.exe", "setup.exe", "MicrosoftEdgeUpdate.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, RegistryValueData, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| sort by Timestamp desc
author: triathIC
tuning_notes: Legitimate software installers frequently write to Run keys. Build an exclusion list of known installer processes and validated RegistryValueData paths.

title: Non-Standard Executables in Run Key Values
description: Surveys all registry Run key values over the past 7 days and highlights entries pointing to executables outside of standard Program Files or Windows directories. Malware typically drops payloads in AppData, Temp, or ProgramData.
kql:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType == "RegistryValueSet"
| where RegistryKey has_any ("\\CurrentVersion\\Run", "\\CurrentVersion\\RunOnce")
| where RegistryValueData !startswith "C:\\Program Files" and RegistryValueData !startswith "C:\\Windows"
| summarize EntryCount = count() by RegistryValueData, RegistryValueName, DeviceName
| sort by EntryCount desc
author: triathIC

title: LSASS Memory Access by Suspicious Process
description: Detects processes accessing lsass.exe that are not standard Windows security components. Direct access to LSASS memory is the primary technique for credential dumping (Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump). This is a critical indicator requiring immediate investigation.
kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where FileName in~ ("procdump.exe", "procdump64.exe", "rundll32.exe", "taskmgr.exe") or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("lsass", "sekurlsa", "MiniDump", "comsvcs")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "lsass" or FileName in~ ("procdump.exe", "procdump64.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsMpEng.exe", "svchost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| sort by Timestamp desc
author: triathIC

title: Credential Dumping Tool Indicators
description: Hunts for command-line artifacts associated with known credential dumping tools including Mimikatz, LaZagne, secretsdump, and reg save of SAM/SECURITY hives. Covers both direct tool execution and living-off-the-land variants.
kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("sekurlsa::logonpasswords", "lsadump::sam", "lsadump::dcsync", "privilege::debug", "token::elevate", "lazagne", "secretsdump", "reg save HKLM\\SAM", "reg save HKLM\\SECURITY", "reg save HKLM\\SYSTEM")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| sort by Timestamp desc
author: triathIC

title: HTTP/S Beaconing Pattern to Single External Host
description: Detects processes making regular HTTP/HTTPS connections to a single external IP at consistent intervals, characteristic of C2 beaconing. The query identifies periodic callbacks by measuring connection regularity over 24 hours.
kql:
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemotePort in (80, 443)
| where ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| where not(ipv4_is_private(RemoteIP))
| summarize ConnectionCount = count(), AvgIntervalSec = avg(datetime_diff("second", Timestamp, prev(Timestamp))) by DeviceName, RemoteIP, InitiatingProcessFileName, bin(Timestamp, 1h)
| where ConnectionCount >= 20
| sort by ConnectionCount desc
author: triathIC
tuning_notes: Exclude known CDN IPs (Akamai, Cloudflare, Azure Front Door) and browser update processes. Adjust ConnectionCount threshold based on network baseline.

title: Uncommon Processes Making HTTP/S Connections
description: Surveys non-browser processes establishing HTTP/HTTPS connections to external IPs over the past 7 days. Highlights unusual executables performing web communication that may indicate C2 channels or data exfiltration.
kql:
let Browsers = dynamic(["chrome.exe", "msedge.exe", "firefox.exe", "iexplore.exe", "opera.exe", "brave.exe"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemotePort in (80, 443)
| where ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| where not(ipv4_is_private(RemoteIP))
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ (Browsers)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("svchost.exe", "MsMpEng.exe", "OneDrive.exe", "Teams.exe", "Outlook.exe")
| summarize ConnectionCount = count(), UniqueIPs = dcount(RemoteIP) by InitiatingProcessFileName, DeviceName
| where ConnectionCount >= 10
| sort by ConnectionCount desc
author: triathIC

title: Certutil Used for Decode or Encode Operations
description: Detects certutil.exe being used with -decode, -decodehex, or -encode flags. Adversaries abuse certutil as a living-off-the-land binary to decode Base64 payloads or obfuscate malicious files.
kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where FileName =~ "certutil.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("-decode", "-decodehex", "-encode", "-urlcache", "-verifyctl")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| sort by Timestamp desc
author: triathIC

title: Processes Spawning from Suspicious Temp or AppData Paths
description: Hunts for process executions originating from Temp, AppData, ProgramData, or Downloads directories. Malware frequently drops obfuscated payloads in these user-writable locations to evade path-based security controls.
kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FolderPath has_any ("\\Temp\\", "\\AppData\\Local\\Temp", "\\AppData\\Roaming\\", "\\ProgramData\\", "\\Downloads\\")
| where FileName !in~ ("chrome.exe", "msedge.exe", "setup.exe", "Teams.exe")
| summarize ExecCount = count(), Devices = dcount(DeviceName) by FileName, FolderPath
| where ExecCount >= 3
| sort by ExecCount desc
author: triathIC
tuning_notes: High false-positive rate in environments with user-installed software. Build a baseline of known legitimate executables in Temp/AppData paths and add them to the exclusion list.

title: Local Account Created on Endpoint
description: Detects local user account creation events (EventID 4720) on Windows endpoints. Local account creation outside of provisioning workflows may indicate an attacker establishing persistence or backdoor access.
kql:
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where EventID == 4720
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, TargetUserName, SubjectUserName, SubjectDomainName, Activity
| sort by TimeGenerated desc
author: triathIC

title: Account Creation and Immediate Privilege Assignment
description: Hunts for patterns where a new account is created and within 1 hour receives role assignments or group memberships. Rapid privilege escalation after account creation is a common attacker pattern during post-compromise activity.
kql:
let NewAccounts = AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName == "Add user"
| extend TargetUPN = tostring(TargetResources[0].userPrincipalName)
| project CreationTime = TimeGenerated, TargetUPN, InitiatedBy = tostring(InitiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName);
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has_any ("Add member to role", "Add member to group")
| extend TargetUPN = tostring(TargetResources[0].userPrincipalName)
| join kind=inner NewAccounts on TargetUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (CreationTime .. (CreationTime + 1h))
| project TimeGenerated, TargetUPN, OperationName, InitiatedBy, CreationTime
| sort by TimeGenerated desc
author: triathIC

title: Security Tool or Service Disabled via Command Line
description: Detects command-line activity that stops, disables, or removes security services including Windows Defender, firewall, and EDR agents. This is a high-priority indicator of defense evasion prior to payload execution.
kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("sc stop", "sc delete", "sc config", "net stop", "Set-MpPreference -DisableRealtimeMonitoring", "netsh advfirewall set", "Uninstall-WindowsFeature", "Remove-MpPreference")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("WinDefend", "MsMpSvc", "Sense", "MpsSvc", "wscsvc", "SecurityHealthService", "DisableRealtimeMonitoring", "advfirewall")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| sort by Timestamp desc
author: triathIC

title: Windows Defender Exclusion Added via PowerShell
description: Hunts for PowerShell commands adding exclusions to Windows Defender (paths, processes, extensions). Attackers add exclusions for their malware staging directories or payload executables to prevent detection.
kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "Add-MpPreference" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("-ExclusionPath", "-ExclusionProcess", "-ExclusionExtension")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| sort by Timestamp desc
author: triathIC

title: Privileged Role Assigned to User or Service Principal
description: Detects assignment of high-privilege Entra ID roles (Global Admin, Privileged Role Admin, Exchange Admin) to users or service principals. Unauthorized role assignments are a primary indicator of account manipulation for privilege escalation.
kql:
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where OperationName == "Add member to role"
| extend RoleName = tostring(TargetResources[0].modifiedProperties[1].newValue)
| where RoleName has_any ("Global Administrator", "Privileged Role Administrator", "Exchange Administrator", "SharePoint Administrator", "Security Administrator")
| extend TargetUPN = tostring(TargetResources[0].userPrincipalName)
| extend InitiatedByUPN = tostring(InitiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, TargetUPN, RoleName, InitiatedByUPN, CorrelationId
| sort by TimeGenerated desc
author: triathIC

title: Service Principal Credential or Certificate Modified
description: Hunts for additions of new credentials (secrets) or certificates to service principals and app registrations. Attackers who gain access to Entra ID add new credentials to existing service principals for persistent backdoor access.
kql:
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has_any ("Add service principal credentials", "Update application – Certificates and secrets management", "Add application credentials")
| extend TargetApp = tostring(TargetResources[0].displayName)
| extend InitiatedByUPN = tostring(InitiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName)
| extend InitiatedByApp = tostring(InitiatedBy.app.displayName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, TargetApp, InitiatedByUPN, InitiatedByApp, CorrelationId
| sort by TimeGenerated desc
author: triathIC
tuning_notes: Legitimate credential rotation will trigger this. Correlate with your org's secret rotation schedule and CI/CD pipeline service principals.
